title: Efficient search for excitable zero-modes in constrained systems
abstract: Kinetically constrained systems, such as those representing Rydberg atom arrays in the blockade regime, have gathered considerable attention due to the presence of atypical eigenstates in their spectrum. The latter manifests itself through the presence of quantum many-body scars as well as unusually large zero-mode (ZM) subspaces which contain analytically tractable eigenstates with various entanglement scalings. In particular, some of the latter are excitable zero-modes (EZMs), meaning that they can be promoted to a non-zero energy for open boundary conditions. In this work, I present an efficient protocol for finding analytical expressions for translation-invariant EZMs in constrained systems, based on the eigendecomposition of the local unconstrained Hamiltonian. I demonstrate the power of this method on a decorated Rydberg chain. In that model, my protocol directly produces a continuous matrix-product-state manifold located entirely in the zero-energy eigenspace for periodic boundary conditions. The span of that manifold grows exponentially with the system, and for odd system sizes it covers the entire zero-momentum eigenspace with zero energy. I then show how the physical structure of the manifold, which is tied to the local eigenbasis, also allows one to derive analytical expressions for ZMs at non-zero momentum and for a polynomial number of exact scars at $E=\pm\sqrt{3}$.
summary: This paper presents a novel, efficient protocol to analytically locate Excitable Zero-Modes (EZMs) in constrained quantum systems, using the local eigenbasis of the Hamiltonian. By applying this to Rydberg chain models, the authors demonstrate the existence of exponentially large zero-mode manifolds and derive explicit formulas for these states under both periodic and open boundary conditions.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop an efficient protocol for finding analytical expressions for Excitable Zero-Modes (EZMs) in quantum many-body systems subject to local constraints.
main_result: The proposed method successfully finds exponentially large families of EZMs in decorated Rydberg chains and demonstrates that the MPS formulation can capture the full eigenspace for non-zero energy states under OBC.
method: The core method involves using the eigendecomposition of the local unconstrained Hamiltonian ($h$) to construct an auxiliary operator ($X$) that dictates the structure of the translation-invariant Matrix Product State (MPS) ansatz.
model_or_system: The study focuses on kinetically constrained systems, specifically modeling Rydberg atom arrays in the blockade regime, analyzed using 1D PXP models and decorated star lattices.
key_observables: Zero-mode (ZM) and Excitable Zero-Mode (EZM) subspaces, the dimension of the zero-mode manifold span, and the energy eigenvalues at non-zero momenta ($E=\pm\sqrt{3}$).
important_parameters: System size ($L$), boundary conditions (Periodic vs. Open), and the blockade parameter regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the local Hamiltonian $h$ has eigenvalues of the form $\{-E, 0, +E\}$ and relies on solving scalar constraints derived from commutation relations.
figures_summary: The notes reference several tables detailing the dimension of the zero-mode manifold span for varying system sizes and boundary conditions, comparing theoretical lower bounds derived from symmetry against actual numerical counts.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the efficient search framework (Section II), applies it to the 1D PXP model (Section III), and then applies the methodology to a more complex decorated lattice structure (Section IV).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the spectral properties of highly constrained quantum systems relevant to Rydberg arrays, providing powerful analytical tools to characterize exotic eigenstates like EZMs.
